blockers.summary: ARITH-B1 — the adjudication denominator: §3 prints 'four records adjudicated' against a numerator of THREE admitting records, and §5 prints the same 'four' against a numerator of TWO. Same quantity, two values, and neither matches the artifacts.
blockers.evidence: §3 (lines 138-142): 'Two trials admit and offer treatment; a third admits and offers enrolment in an observational cohort. Those are counts of the four records adjudicated here, not of the registry.' §5 (line 212): 'Four candidates were adjudicated: two admit, one of them observationally, and two refuse.' The artifacts: research/literature/emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json -> "summary": {"candidates_adjudicated": 4, "admits_and_is_interventional": 1, "admits_but_is_observational": 1, "refused": 2}, and its "adjudications" list is exactly [NCT06571734, NCT04151342, NCT06094101, NCT07188532]. Of THOSE four, exactly ONE admits and offers treatment, not two. The paper's second treating admitter, NCT05918640, is not in that file at all: it is research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.confirmed_fusion_family_defined, a one-element list ({"nct_id": "NCT05918640", "eligibility_text_retrieved": true, "eligibility_basis": "fusion-family-defined (FET: EWSR1 / FUS / TAF15)"}). So §3's numerator (3 admitting: NCT05918640, NCT06571734, NCT04151342) is drawn from a set of FIVE adjudicated records while its denominator is a batch of four that excludes one of them and includes two refusals discussed in §4. The alternative reading — 'here' = §3's own four table rows — is refuted by the paper's own §2: 'The basket records in §3's third row are the exception and are not adjudicated', and that row is nine records, not one. The sentence is therefore wrong under every reading, and it contradicts §5's tally of the same quantity. Provenance of the defect: the clause was appended in commit 8c574fca8 ('Those are counts of the four records / adjudicated here, not of the registry') to a numerator sentence that already read 'Two trials admit and offer treatment; a third admits' — the 4 was typed from the adjudication artifact's summary rather than derived from the records the sentence counts.
blockers.fix: Derive the number instead of typing it. Five records carry an admit/refuse verdict in this paper: NCT05918640 and NCT06571734 admit and treat, NCT04151342 admits observationally, NCT06094101 and NCT07188532 refuse. Either (a) make §3 read 'Those are counts of the five records this paper adjudicates, not of the registry' and make §5 read 'Five records were adjudicated: three admit, one of them observationally, and two refuse', or (b) keep both numbers but scope them explicitly — §3: 'Those are counts of the three records in this table that were adjudicated' and §5: 'Of the four candidates the screens flagged and the 2026-08-09 read adjudicated, one admits and treats, one admits observationally, and two refuse; NCT05918640 was confirmed in the 2026-08-07 read.' blockers.summary: §2 states the transport defect's trigger as the registry ESCAPING comparison operators. The committed fetcher source, which the paper itself cites in §7 as the fix, records that exact account as a hypothesis that was tested and REFUTED: the registry emits LITERAL angle brackets.
blockers.evidence: Paper §2: 'The fetcher passed registry payloads through an HTML stripper, which deletes spans between angle brackets; the registry escapes comparison operators the same way, so eligibility text lost characters'. scripts/lit_fetch_urls.py at the pin, lines 218-228, says the opposite in terms: 'ClinicalTrials.gov emits LITERAL angle brackets inside free-text eligibility criteria — "PLT < 100,000/mcL", "prednisone > 10 mg daily"', followed by '⚠ SUPERSEDED, RETAINED: this comment first said the trigger was HTML-ESCAPED brackets (`<`/`>`). That was wrong and the synthetic written from it did not reproduce the defect — modules survived. The real record settles it: 0 literal `<` and 13 orphaned literal `>` remain in the damaged file, which is the stripper's own footprint.' Both data artifacts the paper rests on carry the same refuted wording (fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json transport_integrity.defect: 'ClinicalTrials.gov escapes angle brackets in free text as backslash-< and backslash->'; emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json transport_integrity.the_known_defect: 'ClinicalTrials.gov escapes angle brackets in free text'), so the paper is faithfully propagating an account the repository has already paid to correct. A methods reader who implements a guard against escaped brackets reproduces the bug — which is precisely what the code comment records happening ('the synthetic written from it did not reproduce the defect').
blockers.fix: Replace 'the registry escapes comparison operators the same way' with 'the registry writes comparison operators as literal `<` and `>` inside free-text criteria, which the stripper reads as tag delimiters'. The same correction is owed to transport_integrity.defect in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json and transport_integrity.the_known_defect in emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json, or the paper should note that those two records carry the superseded account.

blockers.summary: §5 describes the screens that built the candidate pool as 'keyword screens on titles, conditions and interventions' and infers from that description that a trial whose fusion language lives only in eligibility text 'could never enter the pool'. The committed manifest shows two of the three screens are free-text `query.term` searches, and the same artifact contains direct evidence that `query.term` reaches fields well beyond title, condition and intervention. The field list in those URLs is a RETURN-field selector, not a search scope. The stated limitation therefore rests on a false description of the instrument.
blockers.evidence: research/literature/emc-clinical-sweep-c3.json: ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed = 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=%22gene+fusion%22+OR+%22fusion-positive%22+OR+%22FET+fusion%22+OR+%22translocation%22&filter.overallStatus=RECRUITING&pageSize=400&format=json&fields=NCTId%7CBriefTitle%7COverallStatus%7CPhase%7CInterventionName%7CCondition%7CStudyType'; ct_basket_recruiting_fixed is the same shape; ct_sarcoma_recruiting_fixed = 'query.cond=soft+tissue+sarcoma...pageSize=1000' — a CONDITION-only search that never touched titles or interventions, and the screen that actually found the headline trial NCT06571734 (its retrieved_from.source_url in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json). That `query.term` searches beyond the three named fields is proved inside the same artifact: task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.search_url is 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies?query.term=NR4A3&pageSize=100&format=json' and its five returned studies (NCT00733200, NCT02968888, NCT03033953, NCT03139344, NCT05447338) carry no 'NR4A3' string in brief_title, official_title, listed_conditions or interventions — e.g. NCT05447338 is conditions ['Neck Pain'], interventions all myofascial-induction procedures. The paper itself states the same fact two bullets earlier: 'The registry's free-text search reads fields beyond the conditions list.'
blockers.fix: Rewrite the bullet to describe the instruments as committed and stop the inference at what is measured: 'Candidates entered the pool through two free-text term screens (fusion, basket) and one condition screen on soft tissue sarcoma. Which fields the registry's term search covers is not established here — it demonstrably reaches beyond conditions and interventions, since the driver-gene term search returned trials carrying the gene in neither — so we cannot say whether a trial whose only fusion language sits in its eligibility text could enter the pool. The fusion screen returned 400 of a 400-record page and is truncated, which is what makes the counts floors.'

No guard module reads the document. I re-derived and confirmed, at the pin: 400/199/526 screen sizes and 1,159 unique studies (fet-fusion-...-2026-08-07.json -> task_2_widened_search.instruments[0..2].returns and retrieval.unique_studies_indexed); the fusion screen's saturation (its manifest URL carries pageSize=400 and it returned 400, while basket 199/400 and sarcoma 526/1000 did not saturate); NCT06571734 target enrolment 73 and NCT04151342 target enrolment 5500; NCT06571734's seven conditions on 2026-08-09 against ten on 2026-08-07 (the three dropped are 'Ewing Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma Metastatic', 'Sarcoma of Bone'); nine = one master screening protocol + seven DETERMINE arms (one NOT_YET_RECRUITING, NCT07440290) + one separate basket; eligibility text retrieved for three of those nine, two by per-NCT URL (ct_determine_arms, ct_nct03767075_bob) and the third inside the unfielded screen (ct_sarcoma_2026_new); NCT05918640's four listed conditions (three sarcomas + Pediatric Cancer), minimum age 10 Years, sponsor Children's Hospital of Philadelphia, one removal marker with verbatim_sentence_is_transport_clean true; NCT06239272's 42 listed conditions with 'Extraskeletal Myxoid Chondrosarcoma' among them and the verbatim '1-30 years at the time of the biopsy'; twelve lost records (the union of transport_integrity.silently_damaged_records and unparseable_records is exactly 12 unique NCT ids), five recovered elsewhere in the same file (NCT05836571, NCT07695311, NCT07188532, NCT05275426, NCT06094101), three of the remaining seven from the two diagnosis condition searches (NCT00720174 COMPLETED, NCT05355753 TERMINATED, NCT01189253 TERMINATED per research/modalities/emc-hypoxia-therapeutic-status.json); the NR4A3 term search's five studies and their conditions; NCT03767075's status_verified_date '2024-04'; five non-US endpoints with one HTTP 200 (ISRCTN), two 403 (EU CTIS, ANZCTR), one SSL handshake failure (jRCT) and one 404 from a wrong URL (WHO ICTRP); and the ISRCTN chondrosarcoma query's total_count 2. Not one of these is bound to its artifact by any instrument.
p1s.fix: Bind at least the load-bearing quantities the way S46-EIGHT-QUANTITIES-BOUND.md bound the ASO paper's: a guard module that reads the expected values AT RUN TIME from fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json (instruments[*].returns, retrieval.unique_studies_indexed, the lengths of confirmed_fusion_family_defined / molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined / candidates_requiring_eligibility_text_verification, the NR4A3 studies list length, NCT06571734's ten conditions) and from emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json (summary.* and the per-record listed_conditions / estimated_enrollment), then prove each binding by ablation with research/manuscripts/claim_ablation.py. The adjudication tally is the first one to bind: it is the quantity ARITH-B1 just got wrong, and nothing would have caught it.

p1s.summary: No gate anywhere in this repository reads an ISRCTN identifier. Both ISRCTN numbers in §4.1 are correct at this commit, but a mistyped digit would pass every gate — the identical hole `lint_citations.py` records having closed for arXiv in AUT-PD-057.
p1s.evidence: `research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py` -> `PATTERNS` has exactly six kinds: PMID, PMCID, DOI, NCT, GEO, ARXIV. There is no ISRCTN pattern. `git grep -ln "ISRCTN" <pin> -- '*.py' '*.yml' '*.yaml' '*.sh'` returns NOTHING — no linter, no test, no workflow, no script in the tree contains the string. The gate does scan this document (PROSE_SUFFIXES = ('.md',) over `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard`), and its six NCT/PMID identifiers do anchor: all six NCTs and PMID 32967265 appear in tracked `.json` fetch products. The two ISRCTNs are simply invisible to it. The linter's own AUT-PD-057 comment describes this exact state for arXiv before 2026-08-28: "EVERY arXiv IDENTIFIER IN THIS REPOSITORY WAS OUTSIDE THE GATE ENTIRELY — not baselined, not anchored, not counted; simply invisible." Both ids check out today: `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json` records `"id": "ISRCTN07742377"` with the verbatim exclusion criterion and `"id": "ISRCTN60791336"` with "Its exclusion list names 'Chondrosarcoma' as an ineligible subtype".
p1s.fix: Add `"ISRCTN": (r"\bISRCTN(\d{8})\b", r"isrctn\.com/(ISRCTN\d{8})")` to `PATTERNS` in `research/manuscripts/lint_citations.py`. All three ISRCTNs in the tree (ISRCTN07742377, ISRCTN60791336, ISRCTN52235823 — 8 digits each) already appear in `non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json`, so the gate lands green with no ledger baseline; a mutation test flipping one digit must go red.

p1s.summary: Not one number in this paper is bound to any artifact. `lint_consistency.py` scans the document only for superseded-value patterns; `pinned-figures.json` has 99 `artifact_figures` entries and none names this paper or any of its three deposit artifacts.
p1s.evidence: `research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json` lists `research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md` in `targets` (29 entries), which `lint_consistency.check_superseded` uses — that only re-checks the 81 registered `superseded` patterns against it. `check_artifact_figures` is driven by `artifact_figures`, and over its 99 entries the substring counts in the registry are: `trial-reachability` = 1 (the `targets` row only), `fet-fusion-trial-eligibility` = 0, `non-us-registry-sweep` = 0, `emc-clinical-sweep` = 0. So nothing pins 42 conditions, five NR4A3-term studies, 1,159 unique studies, 400/199/526, seven-vs-ten conditions, twelve/five/three/seven damaged records, n=73, n=5500 or age 1-30. The repository's own committed census agrees and quantifies it: `research/manuscripts/claim-coverage.json` records for this document `{"sentences": 87, "covered": 0, "with_a_number": 20, "with_a_number_covered": 0, "uncovered": 87, "uncovered_with_a_number": 20}` — zero of 87 sentences and zero of 20 numeric sentences are read by any instrument. `claim_coverage.py`'s docstring is explicit that this is the remaining blocker risk: "The uncovered set IS the remaining blocker risk".
p1s.fix: Add `artifact_figures` entries with `must_appear_in: ["research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md"]` for at least the four numbers a future edit could silently falsify: NCT06239272's condition count (`fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json` -> `task_1_reverification_of_section_3_3.trials[1].listed_conditions`, len 42), NCT06571734's seven retrieved conditions (adjudication file -> `adjudications[0].listed_conditions`, len 7) against the sweep's ten, the NR4A3 term-search count (`task_2_widened_search.nr4a3_is_absent_from_the_registry_index.studies`, len 5) and `retrieval.unique_studies_indexed` (1159).

p1s.summary: The abstract states the remedy flatly as 'the fix', while §6.1 shows the remedy is unavailable in the gene-family case and demonstrably costly. The abstract-only reader takes away a clean fix the body itself complicates.
p1s.evidence: Abstract: 'the fix is that trials whose eligibility is molecular should list the histologies that molecular criterion admits'. §6.1: 'Where it names a gene family it does not exist: enumerating every histology an EWSR1, FUS or TAF15 criterion admits is an editorial act, not a transcription. NCT07188532 shows the cost, listing *round cell sarcoma with EWSR1-non-ETS fusion* while §4 adjudicates it as refusing this disease.' The adjudication artifact confirms both halves — NCT07188532 listed_conditions = ['Ewing Sarcoma', 'Round Cell Sarcoma With EWSR1-non-ETS Fusion'] and verdict '⛔ DOES NOT ADMIT'. Nothing in the abstract carries the qualification, and nothing reads the abstract against §6, so an edit to either drifts silently.
p1s.fix: Add the qualification to the abstract's 'Why it matters' in one clause: '...should list the histologies that molecular criterion admits — which is a transcription where the criterion names a class and an editorial act where it names a gene family'.

p1s.summary: Every registry figure the previous round added to this paper is correct at the pin and is read by nothing. The manuscript is a pinned-figures TARGET but has zero artifact_figures bindings, so an ordinary edit to either the paper or its source JSON diverges silently.
p1s.evidence: research/manuscripts/pinned-figures.json at the pin lists research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md at targets[14], but a search of its artifact_figures (99 entries), table_completeness, subset_checks and derivations blocks for 'reachability', 'fet-fusion-trial' or 'non-us-registry' returns False in every block. The unguarded, newly-added figures I verified by hand this round: 400/199/526 screen sizes and '1,159 unique studies indexed' (retrieval.unique_studies_indexed = 1159); 'Twelve records were lost ... five of them recoverable ... Three of the remaining seven' (derived from transport_integrity.silently_damaged_records + unparseable_records); 'target enrolment 73' and 'target enrolment 5500' (estimated_enrollment); 'all seven as retrieved 2026-08-09' vs 'the fielded screen ... recorded ten' (two listed_conditions arrays of length 7 and 10); '42 conditions' and 'age 1 to 30 ... at the diagnostic biopsy'; 'NCT03767075 ... RECRUITING flag last verified in April 2024' (status_verified_date = '2024-04').
p1s.fix: Add artifact_figures entries binding at least the load-bearing scalars to their source keys, e.g. {id: 'reach_unique_studies_indexed', artifact: 'research/literature/fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json', key: 'retrieval.unique_studies_indexed', context: '1,159 unique studies indexed', must_appear_in: ['research/manuscripts/care-delivery/emc-trial-reachability.md']}, and the same shape for the two estimated_enrollment values and NCT03767075's status_verified_date.

p1s.summary: The staleness limitation names one stale status flag among the nine molecularly-defined records, but six of those nine carry NO status-verified date in the record at all, because the fields-limited basket screen never requested one. The bullet therefore bounds an exposure that is unmeasured for two-thirds of the group.
p1s.evidence: Paper §5: 'Every status here is as posted on the retrieval date, and one of the nine, the basket trial NCT03767075, carried a RECRUITING flag last verified in April 2024.' In fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, task_2_widened_search.molecularly_defined_not_histology_defined: NCT05768178, NCT05770037, NCT05770102, NCT05770544, NCT05786716 and NCT07440290 each have "status_verified_date": null and "last_update_post_date": null, all with retrieved_from.source_url = the ct_basket_recruiting_fixed URL whose `fields=` list omits statusVerifiedDate. NCT03767075 = '2024-04' and NCT06988475 = '2025-11' are the only dated ones besides NCT05722886 ('2026-06'). That the nulls are field-limitation and not registry absence is provable from the pair: NCT06571734 is null in the 2026-08-07 fielded screen and 'status_verified_date': '2026-06' once re-fetched individually in emc-trial-reachability-adjudication-2026-08-09.json. The same gap exists for three of the four adjudicated records, where only NCT06571734 carries a status_verified_date and the file's own _limits says 'Each record's statusVerifiedDate is quoted where the payload carried one.'
p1s.fix: Add the measured shape to the bullet: 'one of the nine, NCT03767075, carried a RECRUITING flag last verified in April 2024; six of the nine were read through a fields-limited screen that returned no verification date at all, so their staleness is unmeasured rather than recent.'

p1s.summary: The paper's core absence — 'a condition search on their own diagnosis does not return' these trials — is established from each record's conditions FIELD, not from any committed record of what a diagnosis condition search actually returned. The two condition searches on the diagnosis were run once, were transport-damaged, were not re-run after the fix, and their return sets are enumerated nowhere.
p1s.evidence: Every 'EMC listed? no' cell traces to emc_in_listed_conditions:false in fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json / listed_conditions in the 2026-08-09 adjudication. The two diagnosis searches exist — emc-clinical-sweep-targets.json ct_emc_all = 'query.cond=extraskeletal+myxoid+chondrosarcoma&pageSize=100' and ct_myxoid_chondrosarcoma = 'query.cond=myxoid+chondrosarcoma&pageSize=100' — but the artifact records only their FAILURES (transport_integrity.unparseable_records lists NCT00720174/NCT05355753 and NCT00720174/NCT05355753/NCT01189253 under those two payloads) and never their return sets; task_2_widened_search.instruments describes them only as returning 'every study whose CONDITION list names EMC'. The paper states the searches 'were not re-run after the fix'. So no committed artifact shows a diagnosis condition search executing and NOT returning NCT05918640 or NCT06571734; the step from 'the histology is absent from the conditions field' to 'the search does not return it' is the paper's §1 model, not a measurement.
p1s.fix: Say which observation carries the absence: 'Absence here is measured on the listed-conditions field of each retrieved record, which §1 identifies as the field a condition search matches; the return set of a condition search on the diagnosis is not itself committed, and those two searches were not re-run after the transport fix.'

p1s.summary: The abstract's warrant for 'two is a floor' attaches saturation to the screens that found the two admitting trials. Neither of them came from the saturated screen.
p1s.evidence: Abstract: 'the screens that found them match keywords and one of them saturated, so two is a floor.' In fet-fusion-trial-eligibility-2026-08-07.json, NCT05918640.retrieved_from.source_url is the per-NCT URL 'https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT05918640?format=json' (a targeted re-verification of a record already cited in an earlier memo — task_1's own _readme), and NCT06571734.retrieved_from.source_url is the sarcoma condition screen 'query.cond=soft+tissue+sarcoma...pageSize=1000', which task_2_widened_search.instruments records as returning 526 — well under its page limit. The screen that saturated is ct_fusion_recruiting_fixed (pageSize=400, 'returns': '400 recruiting studies...'), and the records it found are NCT07188532, NCT06094101 and NCT04151342 — the two refusals and the observational cohort. §5's fuller statement is the correct one, because truncation of the POOL is what makes the counts floors; the abstract's compression is not.
p1s.fix: Reattach the saturation to the pool: '...and the pool they were drawn from was built by keyword screens, one of which came back at its page limit, so two is a floor.'

p1s.summary: §4.1 says one query ran on the UK registry; two did. And the two registries are compared on findings produced by non-comparable instruments — 1,159 indexed studies through fusion/basket/sarcoma screens on one side, three records from two queries on the other — which the paper does not state when it concludes 'the mechanism therefore runs in both directions'.
p1s.evidence: Paper §4.1: 'the query that ran there was the parent term chondrosarcoma, and it returns two trials'. research/literature/non-us-registry-sweep-2026-08-09.json endpoints[0] records "registry": "ISRCTN (UK)", "queries": ["chondrosarcoma", "sarcoma AND fusion"], and isrctn_what_it_holds carries both query_chondrosarcoma (total_count 2) and query_sarcoma_and_fusion (total_count 1, ISRCTN52235823, a diagnostic methylome study), which the paper never mentions. Against that, retrieval.unique_studies_indexed = 1159 on the US side. So 'In the non-US registry read here the disease appears only as an exclusion' is a within-registry universal drawn from three records returned by two queries, and no ISRCTN instrument comparable to the 400-record fusion screen was run — an admitting-but-not-naming trial there is something the search design had little power to detect. §5 bounds the GEOGRAPHIC generalisation ('not shown to generalise') but says nothing about the asymmetry of the instruments.
p1s.fix: State both: 'Two queries ran there — the parent term chondrosarcoma, returning two trials, and sarcoma AND fusion, returning one diagnostic study. Those three records are the whole of what was read in that registry, against 1,159 indexed on the US side, so the direction of the mechanism there is what three records show and not a property of the registry.'

note: Round 3, five blind seats — arithmetic, citations, hostile, regression, statistics. All five verdicts supported_with_reservations: no lens could break the central claim. 13 blocker entries, 9 P1s, collapsing to five families. FOUR of five seats independently found §3's adjudication count, which prints one denominator against two different numerators and matches neither the artifact nor §5. FOUR of five found §7's data-availability paths, two of which name files that do not exist at the pin while a fourth manifest that ran is omitted. The regression seat reports that THREE of its three blockers are text the previous round's repair pass introduced — the AUT-PD-207 defect class, now measured on a second paper.
